title: Can you structure these 9 growth case questions in two minutes each?
description: 9 growth case prompts to structure in two minutes each, with model answers, where to start and the trap to avoid.
hook: Growth prompts are open by nature, which is exactly why structure matters. These nine come from real-feeling situations across industries. Give yourself two minutes per prompt, then open the model and look for what you missed.
body:
1. How should a newspaper grow digital subscriptions?

Show a model structure
  • Reach: Traffic: search, social, newsletters; New audiences and topics
  • Conversion: Paywall design, trials, price; Sign-up friction
  • Retention: Engagement habits, apps, bundles; Cancellation process and win-back
  • Revenue per subscriber: Tiers, family plans, add-ons; Annual vs monthly

Where to start: The funnel: find the step with the biggest drop-off.

The trap: Only listing marketing ideas without the reach → convert → retain funnel.

2. How can a university attract more international students?

Show a model structure
  • Markets: Which countries have demand; Competition from other countries
  • Offer: Courses, price, scholarships; Rankings and graduate jobs
  • Recruitment: Agents, partners, digital; Conversion from offer to arrival
  • Barriers: Visas and policy; Housing and support

Where to start: Conversion from offer to arrival: many offers are lost to visas and competitors.

The trap: Ignoring visas and housing, which often limit numbers.

3. How can a gym chain grow revenue by 20% in three years?

Show a model structure
  • More gyms: New gyms, new areas; Which cities
  • More members per gym: Better conversion from trials; New segments: corporate, off-peak, older
  • Keep members longer: Churn by month of membership; Onboarding, classes, community
  • More per member: Price, premium tiers, personal training; Retail, nutrition, apps

Where to start: Keep members longer: churn is usually the biggest lever in gyms.

The trap: Only thinking about new members.

4. How can a mobile operator increase revenue per customer?

Show a model structure
  • Price: Plan prices, inflation-linked rises; Fewer discounts on renewal
  • Upgrade: Bigger data plans, 5G; Handset financing
  • Add services: Insurance, streaming bundles, home broadband; Family plans
  • Keep value: Churn of high-value customers; Stop customers moving to cheaper plans

Where to start: Upgrade and add services: price rises are fastest but risk churn.

The trap: Raising prices without checking churn.

5. Should a bubble-tea chain grow by franchising instead of opening its own shops?

Show a model structure
  • Economics for us: Fees and royalties vs own-shop profits; Capital needed
  • Speed: Shops opened per year each way; Our capacity to manage growth
  • Control: Quality and brand consistency; Choosing and supporting franchisees
  • Economics for franchisees: Franchisees' payback; Will good partners sign up?

Where to start: Economics for franchisees: if they can't make money, the model fails.

The trap: Looking only at our royalty income.

6. How can a national museum raise $10M a year more without charging for entry?

Show a model structure
  • Visitors: More visits, longer stays; Tourists vs locals
  • Spend per visitor: Shop, café, paid exhibitions; Donations at the door
  • Other income: Events and venue hire; Licensing images and brand, touring shows
  • Supporters: Memberships, patrons; Corporate partners, grants

Where to start: Paid exhibitions and events: they bring the biggest sums quickly.

The trap: Only thinking about the shop and café.

7. How can a coworking company double revenue in three years?

Show a model structure
  • More space: New buildings, partnerships with landlords; Which cities
  • Fuller space: Occupancy, private offices vs desks; Corporate teams
  • Price: Rates vs rivals; Contract length
  • More services: Meeting rooms, events; Virtual offices, add-ons

Where to start: Fuller space: filling existing buildings costs far less than opening new ones.

The trap: Only opening new locations.

8. How can an airline raise extra revenue per passenger?

Show a model structure
  • Before the flight: Bags, seats, priority boarding; Fare bundles
  • On board: Food, drink, Wi-Fi; Duty free
  • Around the trip: Hotels, cars, insurance; Commission from partners
  • Loyalty: Credit card and points sales; Subscriptions

Where to start: Before the flight: bags and seats bring most extra revenue.

The trap: Charging for everything and hurting customer satisfaction.

9. How can a charity grow its donations by 30%?

Show a model structure
  • More donors: New audiences, digital, events; Cost to acquire a donor
  • Keep donors: Monthly giving, thanking, reporting impact; Why donors stop
  • Bigger gifts: Major donors, legacies; Matching from companies
  • Other sources: Grants, corporate partners; Trading and shops

Where to start: Keep donors: retaining one is far cheaper than finding a new one.

The trap: Only running bigger campaigns.
